column1: # C files deliberately kept inside a library that already has a build.zig.

# leaves C behind has to say so here instead of leaving a parallel tree.
# A .c under a library's tests/ needs no row: C test fixtures are how the Zig
# is held to the C ABI, and they are deliberately C.

column1: # ra8_dfu is partially migrated: the polled USB-DFU host driver is Zig
# (#2809), the boot logic the bootloader runs at reset is Zig (#2918), and
# the root-of-trust verifier is Zig (#2943); four C TUs remain. The two that
# are left of the root-of-trust block (antirollback, launch) are blocked by
# white-box suites that #include the .c files, not by the shared trailer
# record; #2932 has the reading and the porting order.

column3: USBX DFU device class bound to real MRAM through the ux_dcd_ra8_usb bridge. Its seam is the vendored USBX callback surface rather than ra8_usb_host_*, so it ports after the host side proves the pattern (#2809).

Board boot path, kept C in #2987 and ported as its own slice. ra8_add_app selects these by filename out of src/boot/ (an app-local override wins), and the linker script places them; the vector table is a table of weak aliases the image overrides, and system_init runs before anything the host suites can call. Nothing in the host gates sees a section placement or a weak override, so an ARM link is the only thing that would verify a port of them.

column1: # ra8_board_ek_ra8d2 is the first PARTIALLY ported board (#2998). The board
# core went to Zig in #3033 (identity, LEDs, switches, the three GLCDC pin
# tables, the panel straps, xSPI and SDHI routing, the Arduino header), as did
# the dual-core descriptor, USB port routing, bringup, the VCOM console
# stream, the clock profile, the camera, ethernet, audio-USB, touch and PDM
# layers; all of that C is deleted. Everything below is the C that has NOT
# moved yet, with the reason it has not. The flip is still partial because
# the MIPI panel unit compiles beside the archive, and sources.cmake now
# reads that off the filtered source list rather than off the board .c by

column3: J32 MIPI-DSI panel bring-up, all that is left of the old comms unit after #3003 moved the board clock init and the VCOM console to Zig. It instantiates ra8_mipi_dsi_config_t and ra8_mipi_phy_config_t, 308 and 345 lines of type definitions with nested timing and timeout blocks, and nothing available here would catch a mirrored-layout mismatch: no host suite reads the config back, the one suite on this path drives the real HAL against fake MMIO at the register level, and only an ARM link verifies the layout. A silent mismatch mis-programs the D-PHY PLL. Ports when the structs can be read rather than mirrored, or alongside a suite that reads back what was programmed.

Facade and link lifecycle. First slice into this library ported only the TLV envelope; the rest of ra8_c6link ports in later slices of #858, and until then every remaining C file carries a row here rather than a silent parallel tree.
Fixed-capacity slot arena behind the frame ring. Ports with the frame layer in a later slice of #858.
Frame header seal and scan over the SPI/SDIO transport. Ports with the arena in a later slice of #858.
Media-download facade over the protobuf service. Ports with its service and transfer halves in a later slice of #858.
Media-download request/response service. Ports with ra8_c6link_mdl.c in a later slice of #858.
Media-download chunk transfer and resume. Ports with ra8_c6link_mdl.c in a later slice of #858.
Poll pump that drains the transport into the event fan-out. Ports after the frame layer in a later slice of #858.
Request/response correlation; the first caller of the Zig priv_c6link_tlv_* symbols this slice lands. Ports in a later slice of #858.
Wi-Fi control surface over the RPC layer. Ports after the RPC layer in a later slice of #858.
Station-mode join and status over the RPC layer. Ports with ra8_c6link_wifi.c in a later slice of #858.
RAM-backed media-download sink used by the host suites. Ports with the media-download stack in a later slice of #858.
Generated protobuf-c serializer for the media-download messages. Stays C: it is vendored generated output regenerated by protoc-c, not hand-written source, so porting it would fork the generator.
